data.name: Maximina
data.gender_notes: Maximina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin name Maximus, meaning 'greatest'. In Christian tradition, Saint Maximina is a martyr and patron saint of the city of Ravenna, Italy. The name Maximina carries the meaning “Greatest” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Maximina usually hope their child will grow to embody greatest and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength and courage in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Maximina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Greatest.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maximina total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Maximina holds cultural significance for its association with the powerful Roman god Maximus, emphasizing strength, greatness, and leadership. This glorious association was adapted by the Christian church when it named a martyr Saint Maximina, adding a sacred dimension to the name.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Maximina evokes the spiritual meaning of possessing a strong faith, trusting in God's might and limitless love. This name symbolizes one who holds unwavering fortitude, remaining steadfast and dedicated to their beliefs, reflecting the courage and faith of Saint Maximina, the martyr who inspires many even today.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Maximina: God's greatest gift, symbolizing strength and limitless potential in faith. The name Maximina evokes the idea of a powerful and unwavering belief in the divine, inspiring those who bear it to embrace their inner fortitude and face life's challenges with unyielding determination.

historical_references.reference: Maximina the Martyr, also known as Saint Maximilla, was a Christian saint and martyr who lived in the Roman Empire during the late 3rd century. Little is known about her life beyond her martyrdom. According to legend, she was a noblewoman who converted to Christianity and was persecuted and executed during the reign of the Roman Emperor Diocletian.

Another Saint Maximina, also known as Maximina of Thebes, is a Christian saint venerated in the Eastern Orthodox, Roman Catholic, and Anglican Churches. She is believed to have lived in ancient Egypt during the Roman period, around the 4th century. According to hagiography, she was a virgin and was martyred during the reign of Roman Emperor Maximian, along with Saint Theodora and Saint Eutychia.

modern_usage.modern_context: Maximina is a Christian name with roots in ancient Rome, particularly associated with the goddess Mater Dei or Mother of the Gods. In modern contexts, the name Maximina is commonly used in academic research for exploring ancient Roman history and mythology. On social media platforms like Twitter and Reddit, users may share posts about Maximina as a symbol of female empowerment and strength, referencing her historical significance as a goddess and powerful figure. Academia.edu, an online research platform, hosts numerous studies and articles on Maximina and related Roman goddesses.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Mary Maximina in Dublin, Ireland credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Maximina, which means "Greatest". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
